title: Iridescent Gear Forge — Custom Shader Pipeline
description: The user operates a mystical forge where interlocking gears drive an iridescence transfer process onto an abalone shell. By adjusting shader uniforms through interactive controls — chromatic shift, fresnel intensity, noise distortion, rotation speed, metallic roughness, and emission pulse — the user sculpts a unique iridescent shader effect that visually flows from the spinning gears onto the shell surface in real time.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads both 'shared_assets/gears.glb' and 'shared_assets/IridescenceAbalone.glb' using GLTFLoader. Position the gears model on the left (-2, 0, 0) and the abalone shell on the right (2, 0, 0). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 7) looking at origin, with OrbitControls enabled. Add an AmbientLight (intensity 0.3) and a DirectionalLight from (5, 5, 5) with intensity 1.5, plus a PointLight at (0, 1, 0) with color #88ccff.

Write a custom ShaderMaterial applied to ALL meshes of the abalone model. The vertex shader should pass worldNormal, viewDirection, and worldPosition to the fragment shader. The fragment shader must implement: (1) a Fresnel-based iridescence effect using a uniform 'uFresnelPower' (range 0.5-5.0), (2) chromatic hue shifting via uniform 'uHueShift' (0-6.28), (3) a simplex noise distortion controlled by 'uNoiseScale' (0.1-3.0) that warps the iridescence pattern, (4) metallic roughness blending via 'uRoughness' (0.0-1.0), and (5) an emission pulse uniform 'uEmissionPulse' (0.0-2.0) that adds a time-based glow synced to gear rotation.

Animate the gears model to rotate around Y-axis at a speed controlled by uniform 'uGearSpeed' (0.1-3.0). Create a visible energy stream between the gears and abalone using a line or particle trail whose color matches the current iridescence output.

Build an HTML/CSS overlay panel with 6 labeled sliders: Hue Shift, Fresnel Power, Noise Distortion, Gear Speed, Roughness, and Emission Pulse. Each slider updates its corresponding uniform in real time. Add a 'Randomize All' button that animates all parameters to random values over 0.5 seconds. Add a 'Reset' button restoring defaults. Validate that all parameters stay within their defined ranges. Display current RGB output of the dominant iridescence color as a hex code below the sliders. The render loop must update time-based uniforms each frame for animated noise and emission pulsing.
